$comment: THE GATE REGISTRY (pc-01db). This file is not a description of the gates —
it is what runs them. dev/gates.py is the only caller, dev/hooks/pre-commit
calls dev/gates.py, and the scheduled agent calls it too. An entry that is
wrong therefore fails loudly instead of lying quietly, which is the whole
point: BP23 in the practice catalog names a guard registry maintained by
the people who installed the guards as erring toward CLAIMING enforcement,
and the audit of one such registry corrected two rows that read as enforced
when the hook had never been enabled in any clone. A registry that only
describes reproduces that fault. This one executes.
ADDING OR REMOVING A GATE REQUIRES EDITING THIS FILE, and that requirement
is enforced, not requested: `dev/gates.py --audit` scans the discovery
globs below and refuses when a gate-shaped file on disk has no entry here,
or when an entry names a file that does not exist. The audit runs inside
pre-commit, so the drift is caught at the commit that introduces it. This
is GP28's coverage axis (does a check exist AND run in the runner) applied
to the gate set itself, which is VP21.
`redcase` is the VP21 denominator: the test that proves this gate can turn
RED. null means unproven, and `--audit` reports the proportion rather than
rounding it up. A gate with no red-case arm is not known to be a gate.
INLINE GATES (pc-fff0, v2.7). Seven enforcement blocks live inside
dev/hooks/pre-commit itself, outside the discovery globs, and this
file's promise - adding or removing a gate requires editing it - was
silently false for them: deleting an inline block changed neither the
audit nor any commit verdict. Each is now registered with `inline`,
the `hook` path, and one `marker` per refusal line it prints. The
audit reads the hook from the INDEX and refuses in both directions: a
registered marker gone from the hook is a removed gate; a refusal
line no marker covers is an added, unregistered one.
THE CLAIM JOIN (pc-fc37, round-7 lane D-F2). README says the state of
every project claim lives in claims.yaml "and nowhere else", and the
editor-debris commit gate had its state, red case and tests only here
and in tests/ - no entry there, and no checker compared the two
registries, so both audited clean over the split. Six of the seven
inline hook gates already carried an entry, which settles the scope
question: inline gates are IN. So every entry names in `claim` the
claims.yaml id it enforces, or states in `claim_why_not` why it
enforces none, and `--audit` refuses a name that ledger does not carry
- reading the ledger from the INDEX under --index, like every other
input. The reverse direction was already covered: a deleted gate file
is a DANGLING ENTRY, a deleted entry an UNREGISTERED GATE.

why: A gate is named for what it is. The naming convention is what makes
discovery possible at all — dev/report.py, dev/claims-edit.py and
dev/claims-ref.py are tools, not gates, and do not match. A new gate
that dodges the convention to dodge the audit is a deliberate act and
will read as one in review.

gates.why: Is claims.yaml well-formed, and does each tier obey the honesty rules it implies?
Is the STAGED ledger structurally sound (E001-E009, E011-E017) against the STAGED config?
on_fail: Exit 0 means WELL-FORMED, never true (spec/format-v1.md rule 1).

gates.why: Is an E-code or spec amendment level allocated twice, or the generated registry stale?
on_fail: A code or amendment level is allocated twice, or the generated

gates.why: Does README prose outrun the claim tier it projects, or does a referral dangle?
on_fail: README prose outruns the claim it projects, or a referral dangles.

gates.why: Is every ledger line valid against spec/record.schema.json (single-record shape)?
precommit_why_not: NOT YET — and 'not yet' is the ruling, not 'no'. It is to be
enabled once it is set up right; the work is pc-9690.
WHAT MEASUREMENT SAID ABOUT ENABLING IT AS-IS. Cost was never the
objection: it runs in 0.2s. The objection is that it caught NOTHING
at commit time that `pecia check` does not already catch. Nine
single-record mutations (type outside the enum, priority out of
range, priority/rev/labels as the wrong JSON type, status outside
the enum, malformed date, empty title) were put to both gates: both
rejected all nine, and both ACCEPTED an unknown extra field. Zero
unique catches. Turning it on in that shape would be a paid step
protecting no invariant already unprotected at that point — GP37
(decision-relevant parsimony) and BP26 (process theater).
WHAT SET UP RIGHT MEANS. Its value is the one thing the overlap
makes possible and nothing currently uses: it is an INDEPENDENT
implementation — a published JSON Schema read by the jsonschema
library — of a judgement pecia's hand-rolled checker also makes.
GP28 keeps an independent observation that must agree and CHECKS
it, because the disagreement carries information a deduplicated
field would destroy; and a second implementation is the
pseudo-oracle that can catch a GENERATOR bug, which a `--check`
structurally cannot. So the commit gate to build is 'do these two
verdicts disagree on any record?' — not this one run twice. Flip
this to true when pc-9690 lands that, with a red-case arm proving
the differential can fire.
Probe scope, stated so it is not overread: 9 mutations, all in
single-record shape — schema-check's own declared territory, which
is where overlap was most likely. A shape violation it alone
catches may exist; none was found. The unknown-extra-field result
is a SHARED blind spot, which a differential cannot see either.

gates.why: Do the ledger-algebra theorems hold, the traps still fail, and the seeded kills still fire?
precommit_why_not: Bounded model-checking over three Alloy files; needs a JDK and the
pinned jar, and costs far more than a commit should. It carries its
own null arm (seeded-kills must FAIL), so it is the one gate in this
registry whose vacuity check is inside the gate rather than beside it.

gates.why: Is the enforcement ACTIVE in THIS clone — hooksPath wired, gates reachable? Posture, never correctness.
precommit_why_not: Answers a question about the clone, not about the commit. Running it
from inside the hook is also near-circular: the hook only runs at all
when the posture it checks is already correct, so it would be a gate
that can never observe its own failure case (VP4).

gates.why: Does the implementation still do what its tests say it does?
precommit_why_not: Ninety seconds across twelve workers (nine minutes serial). A commit gate that
costs minutes is a commit gate people learn to bypass, which is worse than not
having it; the loop and the hook's fast gates cover commits, this covers rounds.

gates.why: Refuse secret-bearing filenames (.env, *.key, *.pem, secrets.*) entering the commit, renames included.

redcase_mutation.why: the refusal block never runs, while every registered marker stays in the hook

gates.why: Refuse every commit while editor debris (swap files, backups) is TRACKED in the index (pc-f0a3).

gates.why: Scan staged additions for key-shaped strings and refuse with the value redacted.
markers: staged change contains a likely secret

redcase_mutation.why: the refusal block never runs, while every registered marker stays in the hook

gates.why: Refuse a staged DELETION of a canonical gate input (set derived from gates.py --canonical-paths; fails closed when it cannot enumerate).
markers: cannot enumerate the canonical gate inputs
refusing staged deletion of canonical file

redcase_mutation.why: the deletion loop iterates over nothing, so no canonical path is ever checked and both markers stay in the hook

gates.why: The manifest must declare the intended branch and it must match HEAD (pc-3303).
markers: the manifest declares what to commit but not where

redcase_mutation.why: the branch declaration is never read, so a manifest naming another branch is never compared with HEAD

gates.why: When .git/EXPECTED_COMMIT exists, every staged path must match a manifest line; consumed only on success.
markers: staged files outside the declared manifest

redcase_mutation.why: the staged set is never compared with the manifest, so an undeclared path commits silently
